question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
solution:
**Given:**

A train crosses two persons in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec respectively

Speed of the two persons is 4 km/h and 6 km/h 

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be S and its length be L 

Now, it crosses first person in 12 sec i.e. (12)/(3600) = (1)/(300) h at 4 km/h

Relative speed ,as they move in the same direction = S - 4 

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time 

⇒ L = ( S - 4 ) × (1)/(300) ..............(1)

Also, it crosses second person in 14 sec i.e. (14)/(3600 ) = (7)/(1800) h at 6 km/h 

Relative speed = S - 6

⇒ L = ( S - 6 ) × (7)/(1800) ............(2) 

From equation (1) and (2) we get 

⇒ (S - 4) × (1)/(300) = (S - 6) × (7)/(1800 )

⇒ ( S - 4 ) = ( S - 6 ) × (7)/(6 )

⇒ 6S - 24 = 7S - 42 

⇒ S = 18 km/h 

**Hence, speed of the train is 18 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Let the speed of the train = y km/hr

Distance = Speed × Time

A train passes a man or a pole covered its length so the distance covered by the train is the same in both cases.

⇒ (y - 4) × 12 = (y - 6) × 14

⇒ 6y - 24 = 7y - 42

⇒ y = 18

**∴ The speed of the train is 18 km/hr.**
